normative.obligation: The protocol relies on Ethernet hardware addresses being 48 bits wide, which is what makes a hardware address length of 6 correct.

normative.quote: ares_op$REQUEST (= 1, high byte transmitted first)

normative.obligation: The 16-bit Ethernet type field of an address resolution packet carries the value ether_type$ADDRESS_RESOLUTION.

normative.obligation: The first field of the packet data is a 16-bit ar$hrd field naming the hardware address space.

normative.quote: 16.bit: (ar$pro) Protocol address space.
normative.obligation: The second field of the packet data is a 16-bit ar$pro field naming the protocol address space.

normative.obligation: On Ethernet hardware the value of ar$pro is drawn from the set of Ethernet protocol type field values.

normative.quote: 8.bit: (ar$hln) byte length of each hardware address
normative.obligation: The third field of the packet data is an 8-bit ar$hln field giving the byte length of each hardware address in the packet.

normative.quote: 8.bit: (ar$pln) byte length of each protocol address
normative.obligation: The fourth field of the packet data is an 8-bit ar$pln field giving the byte length of each protocol address in the packet.

normative.quote: 16.bit: (ar$op)  opcode (ares_op$REQUEST | ares_op$REPLY)
normative.obligation: The fifth field of the packet data is a 16-bit ar$op opcode field holding either ares_op$REQUEST or ares_op$REPLY.

normative.quote: nbytes: (ar$sha) Hardware address of sender of this packet, n from the ar$hln field.
normative.obligation: The sixth field of the packet data is ar$sha, the sender's hardware address, occupying exactly as many bytes as ar$hln states.

normative.quote: mbytes: (ar$spa) Protocol address of sender of this packet, m from the ar$pln field.
normative.obligation: The seventh field of the packet data is ar$spa, the sender's protocol address, occupying exactly as many bytes as ar$pln states.

normative.quote: nbytes: (ar$tha) Hardware address of target of this packet (if known).
normative.obligation: The eighth field of the packet data is ar$tha, the target's hardware address if known, occupying exactly as many bytes as ar$hln states.

normative.quote: mbytes: (ar$tpa) Protocol address of target.
normative.obligation: The ninth and last field of the packet data is ar$tpa, the target's protocol address, occupying exactly as many bytes as ar$pln states.

normative.quote: routing determines the protocol address of the next hop for the packet and on which piece of hardware it expects to find the station with the immediate target protocol address
normative.obligation: The generation path relies on routing having already supplied the next-hop protocol address and the piece of hardware on which that station is expected.

normative.quote: some lower layer (probably the hardware driver) must consult the Address Resolution module ... to convert the <protocol type, target protocol address> pair to a 48.bit Ethernet address
normative.obligation: Before an Ethernet packet can be transmitted, a lower layer must consult the Address Resolution module to convert the <protocol type, target protocol address> pair into a 48-bit Ethernet address.

normative.quote: The Address Resolution module tries to find this pair in a table.
normative.obligation: On being consulted, the Address Resolution module looks the <protocol type, target protocol address> pair up in its translation table.

normative.quote: If it finds the pair, it gives the corresponding 48.bit Ethernet address back to the caller
normative.obligation: When the lookup succeeds, the module returns the corresponding 48-bit Ethernet address to the caller.

normative.quote: (hardware driver) which then transmits the packet
normative.obligation: On receiving the resolved address, the caller transmits the pending packet to it.

normative.quote: If it does not, it probably informs the caller that it is throwing the packet away
normative.obligation: When the lookup fails, the module discards the packet awaiting transmission.

normative.quote: it probably informs the caller that it is throwing the packet away (on the assumption the packet will be retransmitted by a higher network layer)
normative.obligation: On discarding the packet the module informs the caller that the packet is being thrown away.

normative.quote: generates an Ethernet packet with a type field of ether_type$ADDRESS_RESOLUTION
normative.obligation: On a lookup failure the module generates an Ethernet packet whose Ethernet type field is ether_type$ADDRESS_RESOLUTION.

normative.quote: The Address Resolution module then sets the ar$hrd field to ares_hrd$Ethernet
normative.obligation: In the generated request the module sets ar$hrd to ares_hrd$Ethernet.

normative.quote: ar$pro to the protocol type that is being resolved
normative.obligation: In the generated request the module sets ar$pro to the protocol type whose address is being resolved.

normative.quote: ar$hln to 6 (the number of bytes in a 48.bit Ethernet address)
normative.obligation: In a request generated for 10Mbit Ethernet the module sets ar$hln to 6.

normative.quote: ar$pln to the length of an address in that protocol
normative.obligation: In the generated request the module sets ar$pln to the byte length of an address in the protocol being resolved.

normative.quote: ar$op to ares_op$REQUEST
normative.obligation: In the generated request the module sets ar$op to ares_op$REQUEST.

normative.quote: ar$sha with the 48.bit ethernet address of itself
normative.obligation: In the generated request the module sets ar$sha to its own 48-bit Ethernet address.

normative.quote: ar$spa with the protocol address of itself
normative.obligation: In the generated request the module sets ar$spa to its own protocol address.

normative.quote: ar$tpa with the protocol address of the machine that is trying to be accessed
normative.obligation: In the generated request the module sets ar$tpa to the protocol address of the machine being accessed.

normative.quote: It does not set ar$tha to anything in particular, because it is this value that it is trying to determine.
normative.obligation: In the generated request ar$tha is left unconstrained, and a receiver may not rely on its content.

normative.quote: It could set ar$tha to the broadcast address for the hardware (all ones in the case of the 10Mbit Ethernet) if that makes it convenient for some aspect of the implementation.
normative.obligation: The module is permitted to set ar$tha of a generated request to the hardware broadcast address.

normative.quote: It then causes this packet to be broadcast to all stations on the Ethernet cable originally determined by the routing mechanism.
normative.obligation: The generated request is broadcast to all stations on the piece of hardware that routing selected.

normative.quote: When an address resolution packet is received, the receiving Ethernet module gives the packet to the Address Resolution module
normative.obligation: A received address resolution packet is handed by the Ethernet module to the Address Resolution module for processing.

normative.quote: Negative conditionals indicate an end of processing and a discarding of the packet.
normative.obligation: Whenever any test in the reception algorithm fails, processing ends and the received packet is discarded.

normative.quote: ?Do I have the hardware type in ar$hrd?
normative.obligation: On reception the module tests whether it supports the hardware type named in ar$hrd, and proceeds only if it does.

normative.quote: [optionally check the hardware length ar$hln]
normative.obligation: The module is permitted, but not required, to check the hardware address length in ar$hln at this point.

normative.quote: ?Do I speak the protocol in ar$pro?
normative.obligation: On reception the module tests whether it speaks the protocol named in ar$pro, and proceeds only if it does.

normative.quote: [optionally check the protocol length ar$pln]
normative.obligation: The module is permitted, but not required, to check the protocol address length in ar$pln at this point.

normative.quote: Merge_flag := false
normative.obligation: The module initialises Merge_flag to false before examining the translation table.

normative.quote: If the pair <protocol type, sender protocol address> is already in my translation table, update the sender hardware address field of the entry with the new information in the packet
normative.obligation: If the <protocol type, sender protocol address> pair is already in the translation table, the module overwrites that entry's hardware address with the sender hardware address from the packet.

normative.quote: and set Merge_flag to true.
normative.obligation: When such an existing entry is updated, the module sets Merge_flag to true.

normative.quote: ?Am I the target protocol address?
normative.obligation: The module tests whether ar$tpa is its own protocol address, and proceeds only if it is.

normative.quote: If Merge_flag is false, add the triplet <protocol type, sender protocol address, sender hardware address> to the translation table.
normative.obligation: When the module is the target and Merge_flag is false, it adds the <protocol type, sender protocol address, sender hardware address> triplet to the translation table.

normative.quote: ?Is the opcode ares_op$REQUEST?
normative.obligation: The module tests whether ar$op is ares_op$REQUEST, and generates a reply only if it is.

normative.quote: (NOW look at the opcode!!)
normative.obligation: The opcode is examined only after the sender information has been merged into or added to the translation table, not before.

normative.quote: Swap hardware and protocol fields, putting the local hardware and protocol addresses in the sender fields.
normative.obligation: To build the reply the module swaps the sender and target hardware and protocol fields, placing its own hardware and protocol addresses in the sender fields.

normative.quote: Set the ar$op field to ares_op$REPLY
normative.obligation: In the reply the module sets ar$op to ares_op$REPLY.

normative.quote: Send the packet to the (new) target hardware address
normative.obligation: The reply is sent to the new target hardware address rather than broadcast.

normative.quote: on the same hardware on which the request was received
normative.obligation: The reply is sent on the same piece of hardware on which the request arrived.

normative.quote: if an entry already exists for the <protocol type, sender protocol address> pair, then the new hardware address supersedes the old one
normative.obligation: A newly received sender hardware address replaces the previously stored hardware address for the same <protocol type, sender protocol address> pair.

normative.quote: The ar$hrd and ar$hln fields allow this protocol and packet format to be used for non-10Mbit Ethernets.
normative.obligation: The ar$hrd and ar$hln fields parameterise the packet format so that the same protocol works on hardware other than 10Mbit Ethernet.

normative.quote: <ar$hrd, ar$hln> takes on the value <1, 6>.
normative.obligation: On 10Mbit Ethernet the pair <ar$hrd, ar$hln> carries the values 1 and 6.

normative.quote: other hardware networks, the ar$pro field may no longer correspond to the Ethernet type field
normative.obligation: On hardware other than Ethernet, ar$pro is permitted to hold values that are not Ethernet protocol type field values.

normative.quote: but it should be associated with the protocol whose address resolution is being sought
normative.obligation: On non-Ethernet hardware the value placed in ar$pro should identify the protocol whose address resolution is being sought.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: Periodic broadcasting is definitely not desired.
normative.obligation: An implementation does not periodically broadcast its address resolution information; information is distributed only as it is needed.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: This format does not allow for more than one resolution to be done in the same packet.
normative.obligation: A single address resolution packet carries exactly one resolution; multiple resolutions may not be multiplexed into one packet.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: a reply has the same length as a request
normative.obligation: A reply packet is the same length as the request that provoked it.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: The value of the hardware field (ar$hrd) is taken from a list for this purpose.
normative.obligation: The value placed in ar$hrd is drawn from the assigned list of hardware address space values, not chosen freely.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: Currently the only defined value is for the 10Mbit Ethernet (ares_hrd$Ethernet = 1).
normative.obligation: The hardware address space enumeration has exactly one defined value at the time of writing, 1 for 10Mbit Ethernet.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: the length of a protocol address should be determined by the hardware type (found in ar$hrd) and the protocol type (found in ar$pro)
normative.obligation: Address lengths should be derivable from the hardware type and the protocol type rather than depending on the length fields.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: It is included for optional consistency checking, and for network monitoring and debugging
normative.obligation: An implementation is permitted, but not required, to use the length fields for consistency checking.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: The opcode is to determine if this is a request (which may cause a reply) or a reply to a previous request.
normative.obligation: A request may cause a reply to be generated, and a reply is a response to a previous request; the opcode is what distinguishes the two.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: The sender hardware address and sender protocol address are absolutely necessary.
normative.obligation: Every address resolution packet must carry the sender hardware address and the sender protocol address.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: The target protocol address is necessary in the request form of the packet so that a machine can determine whether or not to enter the sender information in a table or to send a reply.
normative.obligation: A request must carry the target protocol address, because the receiver decides from it whether to record the sender and whether to reply.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: It is not necessarily needed in the reply form if one assumes a reply is only provoked by a request.
normative.obligation: The design relies on a reply being produced only in response to a request.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: Its meaning in the reply form is the address of the machine making the request.
normative.obligation: In a reply, ar$tha holds the hardware address of the machine that made the request.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: There are no padding bytes between addresses.
normative.obligation: The address fields are packed with no padding bytes between them.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: The packet data should be viewed as a byte stream in which only 3 byte pairs are defined to be words (ar$hrd, ar$pro and ar$op)
normative.obligation: The packet data is a byte stream in which only ar$hrd, ar$pro and ar$op are two-byte words.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: which are sent most significant byte first (Ethernet/PDP-10 byte style)
normative.obligation: The three word fields ar$hrd, ar$pro and ar$op are transmitted most significant byte first.

normative.quote: When a monitor receives an Address Resolution packet, it always enters the <protocol type, sender protocol address, sender hardware address> in a table.
normative.obligation: A monitor enters the sender triplet of every received address resolution packet into its table, without applying the target protocol address test.

normative.quote: If a host moves, any connections initiated by that host will work, assuming its own address resolution table is cleared when it moves.
normative.obligation: Recovery for a host that moves relies on that host clearing its own address resolution table when it moves.

normative.quote: 48.bit Ethernet addresses are supposed to be unique and fixed for all time, so they shouldn't change.
normative.obligation: The protocol relies on 48-bit Ethernet addresses being unique and never changing.

normative.quote: there is always the danger of incorrect routing information accidentally getting transmitted through hardware or software error; it should not be allowed to persist forever
normative.obligation: Incorrect information in the translation table should not be allowed to persist indefinitely.

normative.quote: Perhaps failure to initiate a connection should inform the Address Resolution module to delete the information on the basis that the host is not reachable
normative.obligation: A failure to initiate a connection should cause the corresponding translation table entry to be deleted.

normative.quote: Or perhaps receiving of a packet from a host should reset a timeout in the address resolution entry used for transmitting packets to that host
normative.obligation: Receiving a packet from a host should reset the timeout on the translation table entry used to transmit to that host.

normative.quote: if no packets are received from a host for a suitable length of time, the address resolution entry is forgotten
normative.obligation: A translation table entry is discarded when no packet has been received from that host for a suitable length of time.

normative.quote: on a perfect Ethernet where a broadcast REQUEST reaches all stations on the cable, each station will be get the new hardware address
normative.obligation: A broadcast request that reaches every station causes every station holding an entry for the sender to take up the new hardware address.

normative.quote: Another alternative is to have a daemon perform the timeouts.  After a suitable time, the daemon considers removing an entry.
normative.obligation: A daemon may perform table timeouts, considering an entry for removal after a suitable time has passed.

normative.quote: It first sends ... an address resolution packet with opcode REQUEST directly to the Ethernet address in the table.
normative.obligation: Before removing an entry the daemon sends a REQUEST directly (not broadcast) to the Ethernet address held in that entry.

normative.quote: (with a small number of retransmissions if needed)
normative.obligation: The daemon retransmits that probe request a small number of times if the first attempt draws no answer.

normative.quote: If a REPLY is not seen in a short amount of time, the entry is deleted.
normative.obligation: If no reply to the probe arrives within a short time, the daemon deletes the table entry.

normative.quote: Since hosts don't transmit information about anyone other than themselves
normative.obligation: A host transmits address resolution information only about itself, never about other hosts.

normative.quote: Perhaps manually resetting (or clearing) the address mapping table will suffice.
normative.obligation: Stale mappings may be cleared by manually resetting the address mapping table.
